| Name | Reason |
|---|---|
| Acutaas Chemicals | ₹32k cr at a P/E of 73.5. The reverse DCF implies about 31% EPS CAGR for 10 years, so it is priced for perfection. |
| Neuland Labs | ₹27k cr at a P/E of 60. Quarters are lumpy (OPM swings between 12% and 40%), so the trend is not sustained. |
| Sansera Engineering | ₹29.6k cr at a P/E of 72 with ROCE of about 15%. Too expensive. |
| Happy Forgings | High quality (31% OPM), but a P/E of 49 at ₹17k cr already prices that in. DIIs are trimming (17.1% → 14.9%). |
| Shivalik Bimetal | Best growth in the set (Q2 sales +45% YoY). But a P/E of 47 implies about 25% CAGR. DIIs cut from 21.1% to 10.9% in two quarters, and debtor days rose to 99. **Watchlist.** |
| Caplin Point | Debtor days have risen every year, from 12 to 138. Receivables are LatAm-heavy. |
| Marksans Pharma | Near-miss: P/E 24, ROCE 19%. But the cash conversion cycle has stretched to 261 days, borrowings went from 30 to 465, and FII holding swings (8% → 19%). |
| eClerx | Near-miss on quality (ROCE 34%, P/E 19). But debtor days went from 62 to 90, FIIs are trimming, and it carries IT/AI de-rating risk. |
| Banco Products | **Closest alternate.** P/E 19.4, ROCE 31%, consolidated Q2 profit +19% YoY. But the standalone (India) profit is falling and growth leans on the NRF Europe arm. Borrowings are ₹516 cr and the CCC is 232. Price verified at ₹704.5 (Google) / ₹706.5 (Screener). **Watchlist.** |
| Avanti Feeds | OPM collapsed from 13% to 4.5% in two quarters, a shrimp margin shock. |
| Apex Frozen | ROCE about 10% and Q2 OPM of 4.9%. |
| Supriya Lifescience | OPM fell from 36% to 22% in the last two quarters, and debtor days went from 70 to 97. |
| Aarti Pharmalabs | ROCE about 11%. Borrowings went from 338 to 897 and promoter holding slipped from 44.65% to 39.66%. |
| Hikal | Loss-making in 4 of the last 6 quarters, with ROCE of 3.5%. |
| Vishnu Chemicals | Borrowings doubled (342 → 718), so growth is debt-funded. ROCE is fading (30% → 16%). |
| Fineotex | FY26 CFO was −24 against PAT of 125, and debtor days reached 137 (acquisition-driven). |
| Privi Speciality | About ₹1,000 cr of debt. Promoter holding fell from 74% to 60.6% (stake sale), and P/E is 37. |
| Indo Count | ROCE 8%, debt ₹1,314 cr, P/E 47. |
| Pearl Global | Borrowings went from 463 to 1,218, OPM is about 10%, promoter holding is slipping, and P/E is 35. |
| Gokaldas Exports | ROCE 7.7%. FIIs halved (26.5% → 13.4%) and debt is ₹1,101 cr. |
| GNA Axles | Promoter holding fell from 68.4% to 58.5% in two quarters. Debtor days are 151 and ROCE is 14%. |
| Sharda Motor | A domestic business, not an exporter. OPM is sliding (14% → 10%). |
| Frontier Springs | Domestic railways, outside the theme. |
| Mastek | Cheap at a P/E of about 10.6, but OPM slid from 17% to 14% and FIIs fell from 11.2% to 5.9%. Exposed to the UK public sector. **Contrarian watch.** |
| R Systems | P/E of about 13, with acquisition-led growth of about 30%. DIIs went from 9.4% to 4.65%, and there is a Blackstone overhang. **Contrarian watch.** |
| Saksoft / Nucleus / Sasken | Revenue flat for six quarters / OPM collapsed to 4–7% / CFO negative for two years. |

`case_study:apple-2016-2023-buffett` · tickers US-AAPL · confidence: verified

Berkshire (Combs/Weschler first, then Buffett) started buying in Q1 2016 when Apple traded ~$90-110 pre-2020-split (~$23-27 today) at ~10-11x earnings, ~9x ex-cash, priced as a peaking hardware cyclical after the first iPhone unit decline. Cost: ~$31.1bn for 908m shares (~$34/share avg) per Berkshire. End-2023 ~$198: ~8x from 2016 low, stake worth ~$170bn+. Split [my arithmetic, approx]: EPS ~$2.08 (FY16, adj) -> ~$6.13 (FY23) ≈ 2.9x, helped by ~40% share-count reduction via buybacks; P/E ~11x -> ~30x ≈ 2.8x. So roughly half EPS, half rerating. Drawdowns: Oct 2018-Jan 2019 ~-39%; COVID 2020 ~-31%; 2022 ~-31%. EARLY SIGNAL in 2016: very high retention/upgrade loyalty, Services revenue growing ~20%+ on an installed base >1bn devices, net cash ~$150bn+ funding buybacks, at a market-level multiple. Who caught it: Warren Buffett / Berkshire (documented 13F, letters). Ended: Berkshire sold ~13% in Q1 2024 and ~390m shares in Q2 2024 (~2/3 of stake by late 2024) as P/E reached ~30x with EPS growth single-digit. LESSON: the biggest gain often comes from the market reclassifying a business (cyclical hardware -> consumer franchise/Services toll); once rerated, future returns fall to EPS growth and the same investor may rationally sell.

- **Start → end:** ~$23-27 split-adj (2016) → ~$198 (Dec 2023) (~8x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** ~50/50: EPS x2.9 (buybacks), P/E x2.8
- **Max drawdown:** -39% (2018-19)
- **Early signal:** 10x P/E, Services growth, installed base, buyback capacity
- **Who caught it:** Berkshire Hathaway (Buffett, Combs, Weschler)
- **Ended/stalled:** Berkshire sold ~2/3 in 2024 at ~30x P/E
- **Lesson:** reclassification rerating; sell discipline when multiple is full
- **Sources:** [1](https://fortune.com/2024/08/03/warren-buffett-berkshire-hathaway-q2-earnings-report-stock-sales-apple-stake/) · [2](https://fortune.com/2024/05/04/warren-buffett-berkshire-hathaway-brkb-brka-q1-earnings-apple-stock-sale/) · [3](https://www.irishtimes.com/business/2024/02/15/warren-buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-reduces-its-stake-in-apple) · [4](https://appleinsider.com/articles/24/08/03/berkshire-hathaway-unloaded-more-than-half-of-its-apple-stock-last-quarter)

`case_study:india-psu-rally-2023-24` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, rerating, sector-psu, sector-defence, sector-railways, cyclical

The BSE PSU index rose ~5x from March 2020 to mid-2024 on government capex (~Rs 6 to ~9.5 lakh crore) and a narrative shift from 'value traps' to 'nation-building' stocks. Railway names (RVNL, IRFC) and defence/shipbuilding (Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard, HAL, BEL) posted triple-digit gains; IRFC, a government lender, traded at a large multiple of book and RVNL, a contractor, at high P/Es (levels unverified). Business Standard (2023) found the rally was mainly multiple rerating; in Apr 2025 defence forward P/Es were ~2x their history (HAL ~28x vs ~14x; BEL ~41x vs ~21x). Peak: July 2024. Unwind: BSE CPSE index ~-30% from the July 2024 peak by end-Feb 2025; Mazagon Dock -59% and Cochin Shipyard -52% from July 2024; by late 2025 IRFC, Concor and RVNL were ~-46% and IRCTC ~-40%. The 4 June 2024 election result (no single-party majority) was an early crack (sharp one-day PSU fall, from memory). Defence had sharp rebounds in 2025 (geopolitics), railways briefly in Sept/Dec 2025. Top signals: valuations ~2x history with no matching earnings upgrade, heavy retail and thematic-fund ownership, government OFS selling into strength, high-stake PSUs (82-89% government) with tiny free floats. Lesson: rerating rallies end when multiples hit the ceiling, even when the capex story continues.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| run | BSE PSU ~5x Mar 2020-Jul 2024 |
| peak | Jul 2024 |
| drawdown | CPSE ~-30% by Feb 2025; MDL -59%; railways ~-46% |
| valuation | ~2x historical P/E |
| lesson | rerating ceilings end rallies |
